Alcatraz Island.station: Alcatraz Island — TEST OF THE 'FIRST ON THE PACIFIC COAST' CLAIM
Alcatraz Island.quote: There were no lights or other aids to navigation at that time in the harbors or bays on the Pacific coast of the United States.
Alcatraz Island.establishes: The Board's own baseline. 'That time' is defined two paragraphs earlier as 9 October 1852, when the Board took charge under the act of 31 August 1852. So every Pacific-coast light is a post-1852 Light-House Board creation. Verified against the page image (leaf n228).

Alcatraz Island.station: Alcatraz Island — TEST OF THE 'FIRST ON THE PACIFIC COAST' CLAIM
Alcatraz Island.quote: 376 | Alcatraz | On the island in the harbor of San Francisco, Cal. ... | F. ... 14 | White. | 36 | 166 | [+ 3] | 1854 | ... | Fog-bell, struck by machinery. This light can be seen 12 miles outside of the Heads.
Alcatraz Island.establishes: The Board's own printed Light List, PACIFIC COAST section. The column head is 'When built.' Alcatraz = 1854. CRITICAL: in the same table Point Pinos (No. 370) is ALSO given as 1854, and every other California station is 1855 or later (Point Loma 1855, Point Conception 1855, Farrallon 1855, Point Bonita 1855, Fort Point 1855, Santa Barbara 1856, Humboldt 1856, Crescent City 1856). The Board therefore records TWO California stations built in 1854 and does not rank them. Both pages verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Alcatraz was one of eight Pacific-coast light-houses contracted under the Secretary of the Treasury before the Board existed, each carried at $15,000. The same page's note reads: 'A special transfer of all works connected with the light-house establishment on the Pacific coast was made to the board on December 22, 1852.' Verified against the page image (leaf n94).

Alcatraz Island.quote: The latest reports on the subject announce the completion of the light-house towers on Alcatraz island, and at Fort Point, Bay of San Francisco, Point Pinas, (Monterey,) and on the Farrallones island.
Alcatraz Island.establishes: By the FY1853 report the TOWERS at Alcatraz, Fort Point, Point Pinos and the Farallones were reported complete — but complete is not lighted. The same page states the eight contract light-houses were 'transferred to this office December 22, 1852,' Capt. H. W. Halleck being inspector. Verified against the page image (leaf n192).

Alcatraz Island.quote: By the last account from San Francisco, it appears that the officer charged with setting up the illuminating apparatus has not been able to procure competent persons to perform that service at the Alcatraz light
Alcatraz Island.establishes: Explains why completion of the tower did not mean exhibition of the light: no one competent in San Francisco to set up the apparatus. [OCR text; page image not separately pulled for this sentence.]

Alcatraz Island.quote: Fog-bells are under construction for Point Conception, Fort Point, Alcatraz island, and mouth of the Columbia river.
Alcatraz Island.establishes: Fog-bell for Alcatraz still under construction in the FY1855 report. Verified against the page image (leaf n267).

Alcatraz Island.quote: Fog-bells have been placed at Point Conception, Farralones, Fort Point, Alcatraz island, and Cape Hancock light-houses.
Alcatraz Island.establishes: Alcatraz fog-bell in place by the FY1856 report. Verified against the page image (leaf n602).

Alcatraz Island.quote: At Alcatraz some needful but inexpensive renovations were made.
Alcatraz Island.establishes: Condition report. Verified against the page image (leaf n302).

Alcatraz Island.quote: 370. Alcatras. — On examining this station quite extensive repairs were found necessary, and have been accordingly made, viz: The gallery floor and its iron fastening have been taken up; the brick-work of the tower, from where it passes through the roof of the keeper's dwelling, has been repointed; a coat of cement has been given to the coping of the tower; a new gallery floor has been laid; the boiler iron covering of the lower part of the lantern has been removed, straightened and refitted, the glass-work of the lantern reset, chimneys repointed and plastered; the tower has received a coat of mortar; a drain for the cellar has been constructed.
Alcatraz Island.establishes: The fullest Era-1 physical description of the Alcatraz structure: a brick tower rising through the roof of the keeper's dwelling, with an iron-clad lantern. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Fort Point (= 'Battery Point' in the Boa.station: Fort Point (= 'Battery Point' in the Board's Era-1 usage)
Fort Point (= 'Battery Point' in the Boa.quote: The small light authorized to be placed on Battery point is to serve as a mere harbor or range light, while this is to mark from seaward the entrance to the bay.
Fort Point (= 'Battery Point' in the Boa.establishes: WHY the station existed, and a naming trap: in the Board's Era-1 text 'Battery Point' ALWAYS means the San Francisco fort site (later Fort Point), never Crescent City's Battery Point. Confirmed by the 1858 Light List, which fixes the Farallon position 'from Fort or Battery point, San Francisco bay, Cal.' Verified against the page image (leaf n79).

Fort Point / Battery Point.quote: The light-house authorized and built on Battery Point, Bay of San Francisco, having been taken down to make room for the works of fortification authorized by law at that point, an appropriation, it is believed, should be made for erecting a light of greater power than the one originally authorized for Battery Point, or Point Lobos, the outer entrance of the bay, and an estimate is accordingly submitted in list B.
Fort Point / Battery Point.establishes: The original Battery Point tower was BUILT and then TAKEN DOWN for the fortification (Fort Point) before it was ever lit. Verified against the page image (leaf n198).

Fort Point.quote: 375 | Fort Point | On the south side of the entrance to the harbor of San Francisco, Cal. ... | F. | 12 | White, | 36 | 52 | [+ 5] | 1855 | ... | Fog-bell, struck by machinery.
Fort Point.establishes: Board's Light List: Fort Point 'When built' 1855, fifth-order, light 52 feet above the sea, fog-bell. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Fort Point.quote: The progress of the fortification works at Fort Point, entrance to San Francisco bay, having rendered the removal of the light-house and fog-signal at that point imperatively necessary, steps have been taken to remove the light to a position over the stairway of the fort, and the fog-signal to a point outside the work near the two-gun battery. The work is now in progress, and the new tower, together with suitable quarters for the keepers, will, it is hoped, soon be completed.
Fort Point.establishes: A SECOND removal of the Fort Point light for the fortification, in FY1863 — the light was moved onto the fort itself. Verified against the page image (leaf n166).

Fort Point.quote: At Fort Point, the fog-bell was taken from its original position on a framework in front of the fort and hung on an angle of the fort facing seaward. Slight repairs have been made to the dwelling.
Fort Point.establishes: Relocation of the Fort Point fog-bell onto the fort. Verified against the page image (leaf n302).

Fort Point.quote: 458. Fort Point, entrance to San Francisco Harbor, California. — A bridge has been built from the bluff near the keeper's dwelling to the fort on which the light and fog-bell are placed. Formerly the keepers were compelled to go from the dwelling down steep stairs and up through the fort in order to get to the tower or fog-signal, a very dangerous task during dark and stormy nights.
Fort Point.establishes: Confirms that by 1876 the light and fog-bell stood ON the fort, with the dwelling on the bluff behind. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Point Bonita.quote: In California. — For a light-house to be placed on Point Boneta, San Francisco, $25,000.
Point Bonita.establishes: The original appropriation request. The same paragraph gives the reason: 'The proposed light-house at the entrance to the bay of San Francisco is necessary to the safety of navigators entering that port and bay.' Verified against the page image (leaf n79).

Point Bonita.quote: During the past year, the light-house at Point Bonita has been erected and the light exhibited.
Point Bonita.establishes: Point Bonita first lighted within the year covered by the FY1855 report (report dated autumn 1855). The Board gives no day-date. The same page adds: 'A fog-gun has been placed and put in operation at that point.' Verified against the page image (leaf n267).

Point Bonita.quote: 374 | POINT BONITA | On the point north side of the entrance to San Francisco bay, Cal. ... | F. | 24 | White. | 45 | 306 | [+ 2] | 1855 | ... | Low brick tower rising from keeper's dwelling. Fog-bell struck by machinery.
Point Bonita.establishes: Board's Light List: built 1855, second-order ([+2]), light 306 feet above the sea. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Point Bonita.quote: Guns have been employed on the United States coast, first under the direction of General Bates, engineer of the twelfth district, at Point Bonita, San Francisco Bay, California. The gun at this station consisted of a 24-pounder, furnished by the War Department. The necessary arrangements being made, by the construction of a powder-house, and laying of a platform, and employment of a gunner, notice to mariners was given that after the 8th of August, 1856, a signal-gun would be fired every hour and half hour, night and day, during foggy or thick weather.
Point Bonita.establishes: Exact date the Point Bonita fog-gun went into service: 8 August 1856. Joseph Henry's own retrospective. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Point Bonita.quote: 411. Point Bonita, entrance to San Francisco Harbor, California. — An appropriation for the establishment of a first-class steam fog-signal at this point was made March 3, 1871. The structure was completed, the machinery placed in position, and the signal, a syren, was put in operation May 29, 1872.
Point Bonita.establishes: Date the Point Bonita first-order steam siren began: 29 May 1872. Verified against the page image (leaf n572).

Point Bonita.quote: The light at Point Bonita is 306 feet above the sea. At this height the light is very frequently obscured by a light haze or fog, when at the steam fog-signal there is no fog or haze. Pilots, steamship captains, and others frequently report passing Point Bonita without seeing the light... A good light on this point is very necessary, it being at the entrance of San Francisco Bay and harbor, and an appropriation of $25,000 is asked for moving the present Point Bonita light house to this point.
Point Bonita.establishes: The Board's own reason for moving the Point Bonita light down the headland — the origin of the 1877 lower light. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Point Pinos.quote: The latest reports on the subject announce the completion of the light-house towers on Alcatraz island, and at Fort Point, Bay of San Francisco, Point Pinas, (Monterey,) and on the Farrallones island.
Point Pinos.establishes: Point Pinos tower complete by the FY1853 report. Verified against the page image (leaf n192).

Point Pinos.quote: At the close of the Mexican war, and the acquisition of California, the President gave orders through the General Land Office to the surveyor general of the Pacific coast to reserve, of the public domain on that coast, certain sites for light-houses and other public purposes, among which was the site for a light-house at Point Pinos. An appropriation was made and the light exhibited in 1854.
Point Pinos.establishes: THE ONLY explicit Board statement in these volumes that any California light was exhibited in 1854 — and it is Point Pinos, not Alcatraz. Also gives the origin of the reservation. Verified against the page image (leaf n444).

Point Pinos.quote: 370 | Point Pinos | On the point, south side of the entrance to the harbor of Monterey, Cal. ... | F. | 13 | Gray. | 35 | 91 | [+ 3] | 1854 | ... | Low brick tower rising from keeper's dwelling.
Point Pinos.establishes: Board's Light List: Point Pinos 'When built' 1854, third-order, light 91 feet above the sea. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Point Conception.quote: Major Bache lost no time, after his arrival in California, in taking the necessary steps for remodelling the important light-houses at the Farallones, Point Conception, and Point Loma; all of which, it is expected, are lighted by this time.
Point Conception.establishes: The three 'important' California towers had to be REMODELLED before they could be lit, because the lanterns procured did not fit the contract towers. Verified against the page image (leaf n268).

Point Conception.quote: In the twelfth light-house district, embracing the entire Pacific coast, the light-houses at Point Loma, San Diego, Santa Barbara, Point Conception, Farralones, and Cape Hancock, have been completed and lighted.
Point Conception.establishes: Point Conception (with Point Loma, Santa Barbara and the Farallones) completed and lighted by the FY1856 report. Verified against the page image (leaf n602).

Point Conception.quote: 369 | POINT CONCEPTION | Near the pitch of Point Conception, Cal. ... | Revg. | 0 30 | 23 | White. | 35 | 250 | [+ 1] | 1855 | ... | Low brick tower rising from keeper's dwelling. Fog-bell, struck by machinery.
Point Conception.establishes: Board's Light List: built 1855, FIRST order ([+1]), revolving at 30-second intervals, light 250 feet above the sea, fog-bell. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Point Conception.quote: 405. Point Conception, sea-coast of California. — An appropriation was made March 3, 1871, for the establishment of a first-class steam fog-signal. A thorough examination and survey of the point were made with a view to ascertain the best location for the signal, and the supply of water. The structure has been completed, and the machinery placed in position.
Point Conception.establishes: Point Conception steam fog-signal built under the act of 3 March 1871. Verified against the page image (leaf n571).

Point Conception.quote: 437. Point Conception, sea-coast of California. — The old dwelling at this station is in a bad condition, and the best plan is to pull it down, leaving the tower by itself... As the tower is in the center of the house, the latter having been built around it, when the walls of the house are removed the tower will be isolated and complete in itself. An appropriation of $12,000 is asked for the purpose of building the new dwellings.
Point Conception.establishes: Describes the original form of the station — a tower built inside the dwelling — and the Board's plan to isolate it. Verified against the page image (leaf n846).

Battery Point / Crescent City.quote: The Santa Barbara light-house has been finished, and the light exhibited, and also the light authorized at Crescent City.
Battery Point / Crescent City.establishes: Crescent City light first exhibited in the year covered by the FY1857 report (i.e. the season of 1856, matching the Light List's 'when built 1856'). The Board gives no day-date. NOTE: the Board never calls this station 'Battery Point'. Verified against the page image (leaf n254).

Battery Point / Crescent City.quote: 380 | Crescent City | On the seaward extremity of the island point forming the southern and western side of the harbor. ... | F. V. F. | 1 30 | 14 | Stone . | 35 | 80 | [+ 4] | 1856 | ... | Low brick tower rising from keeper's dwelling.
Battery Point / Crescent City.establishes: Board's Light List: Crescent City built 1856, fourth order, fixed varied by flashes at 1m30s, light 80 feet above the sea; the position description is the Battery Point islet. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Battery Point / Crescent City.quote: 457. Crescent City, sea-coast of California. — This station is in a dilapidated condition, and should be rebuilt if the light is to be continued. The entire wood-work of the keeper's stone dwelling must be removed. The ends of many of the lower floor-timbers are entirely gone, and the floor is held up by shores. But the light itself is of little consequence. No vessel can enter Crescent City harbor at night, and no vessel bound up or down the coast can, with safety, run near enough to make the light. The rocks off Point St. George are one of the chief dangers to navigation on the coast. A first-order light should be placed there. When that is done the Crescent City station should be discontinued.
Battery Point / Crescent City.establishes: The Board's blunt Era-1 verdict on Crescent City: structurally failing and navigationally near-useless; it recommends discontinuance once a St. George Reef light exists. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Humboldt Harbor.establishes: Humboldt was one of the eight $15,000 pre-Board contract light-houses on the Pacific coast. Verified against the page image (leaf n94).

Humboldt Harbor.quote: The light and range at Humboldt harbor will be exhibited about the first of November.
Humboldt Harbor.establishes: The Board's forecast of Humboldt's first lighting: about 1 November 1856. Note it was a LIGHT AND RANGE. Verified against the page image (leaf n602).

Humboldt Harbor.quote: 379 | HUMBOLDT | On the north side of the entrance to Humboldt harbor, Cal. It is 1/4 mile from the inlet, and about midway between the sea and bay shores. ... | F. | 12 | White. | 45 | 53 | [+ 4] | 1856 | ... | Brick tower rising from keeper's dwelling. Fog-bell, struck by machinery.
Humboldt Harbor.establishes: Board's Light List: Humboldt built 1856, fourth order, light only 53 feet above the sea, fog-bell. The low, sand-spit siting is the root of its later troubles. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Humboldt Harbor.quote: The light-house at Humboldt was reported to be in a critical condition by reason of the action of heavy storms and high tides. The peninsula on which this light-house stands is about a half mile wide and but a few feet above the level of the sea, and composed of loose, drifting sand... It is doubtful, however, whether any work except one of a very expensive character can permanently secure the light-house.
Humboldt Harbor.establishes: First Board warning that the site was not tenable. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Humboldt Harbor.quote: In this view of the case the board has under consideration the propriety of removing this light to a point about four miles south of the entrance to Humboldt bay, known as Table bluff. This point is salient, with a firm and permanent foundation for a light-house, and a light there would subserve the purposes of navigation better than where it is now placed; it is not so frequently enveloped in fog as the spit where the light now stands.
Humboldt Harbor.establishes: THE EARLIEST Board statement of the intention that eventually produced the Table Bluff station and the abandonment of Humboldt Harbor. The actual abandonment falls outside the volumes obtained (see 'gaps'). Verified against the page image (leaf n302).

Humboldt Harbor.quote: 452. Humboldt, coast of California. — An appropriation of $10,000 was made by Congress March 3, 1873, for a steam fog-signal at this station. The work was commenced in December of 1873, and was completed in March last... The signal went into operation on the 10th of May last.
Humboldt Harbor.establishes: Humboldt steam fog-signal in operation 10 May 1874; cost $10,000 under the act of 3 March 1873. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Farallon Islands.quote: The distance of the Farrallones, nearly twenty-nine miles, forbids its being of any further use than as an off-shore sea-coast light, and of the greatest importance in that respect.
Farallon Islands.establishes: The Board's statement of the Farallon light's FUNCTION, used to justify a separate light at Point Bonita. Verified against the page image (leaf n79).

Farallon Islands.quote: The latest reports on the subject announce the completion of the light-house towers on Alcatraz island, and at Fort Point, Bay of San Francisco, Point Pinas, (Monterey,) and on the Farrallones island.
Farallon Islands.establishes: Farallon tower complete by the FY1853 report. Verified against the page image (leaf n192).

Farallon Islands.quote: 372 | FARRALLON | On the largest or southeast Farrallon islet, 30 miles south 75° 12' west, true, from Fort or Battery point, San Francisco bay, Cal. ... | Revg. | 1 00 | 26 | Brick. | 29 | 360 | [+ 1] | 1855 | ... | Tower on the highest peak of the rock.
Farallon Islands.establishes: Board's Light List: Farallon built 1855, FIRST order, revolving at one-minute intervals, light 360 feet above the sea, tower on the highest peak. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Farallon Islands.quote: 442. Farallones, off entrance to San Francisco Bay. — The dwelling at this station is very much out of repair, and is much too small for the wants of a first-order station. It was built in 1855 out of rock quarried on the island, and is very damp.
Farallon Islands.establishes: Dates and describes the original Farallon keepers' dwelling: 1855, of rock quarried on the island. The Board repeated this sentence verbatim in 1875 (p. 791) and 1876 (p. 793). [OCR text; not verified against the page image, but the identical sentence appears in three successive reports.]

Santa Barbara.quote: In the twelfth light-house district, embracing the entire Pacific coast, the light-houses at Point Loma, San Diego, Santa Barbara, Point Conception, Farralones, and Cape Hancock, have been completed and lighted.
Santa Barbara.establishes: Santa Barbara completed and lighted by the FY1856 report. Verified against the page image (leaf n602).

Santa Barbara.quote: no title has been obtained to any site on that coast from individuals or corporations, except at Santa Barbara, where the corporate authorities of the town deeded the necessary land to the United States. ... The Santa Barbara light-house has been finished, and the light exhibited, and also the light authorized at Crescent City.
Santa Barbara.establishes: Santa Barbara was the ONLY California site whose title came from a private/corporate grantor in this period — the town deeded it. And the light was 'finished, and the light exhibited.' Verified against the page image (leaf n254).

Santa Barbara.quote: 368 | Santa Barbara | On the point 2 miles south-westerly from Santa Barbara landing, Cal. ... | F. R. | 12 | Gray. | 34 | 180 | [+ 4] | 1856 | ... | RED light. Low brick tower rising from keeper's dwelling.
Santa Barbara.establishes: Board's Light List: Santa Barbara built 1856, fourth order, and originally a RED light 180 feet above the sea. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Santa Barbara.quote: At Santa Barbara some repairs are required to the cellar, and some slight renovation of plastering. The lens apparatus requires the addition of one or more panels, the present arc of illumination being limited to 180°, and vessels approaching outside of this angle cannot see the light.
Santa Barbara.establishes: A defect statement: the Santa Barbara lens covered only 180 degrees. Verified against the page image (leaf n302).

Point Loma (Old).quote: Major Bache lost no time, after his arrival in California, in taking the necessary steps for remodelling the important light-houses at the Farallones, Point Conception, and Point Loma; all of which, it is expected, are lighted by this time.
Point Loma (Old).establishes: Point Loma had to be remodelled before lighting; the Board expected it lit by autumn 1855. Verified against the page image (leaf n268).

Point Loma (Old).quote: In the twelfth light-house district, embracing the entire Pacific coast, the light-houses at Point Loma, San Diego, Santa Barbara, Point Conception, Farralones, and Cape Hancock, have been completed and lighted.
Point Loma (Old).establishes: Point Loma completed and lighted by the FY1856 report. Verified against the page image (leaf n602).

Point Loma (Old).quote: 365 | POINT LOMA | On the west side of the entrance to San Diego bay, Cal. ... | F. | 25 | Dark . | 35 | 457 | [+ 3] | 1855 | ... | Low brick tower rising from keeper's dwelling. Mag. variation 12° 26' east.
Point Loma (Old).establishes: Board's Light List: Point Loma built 1855, third order, light 457 feet above the sea — the highest light in the United States at that date, and the fact that later doomed it to fog. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Cape Mendocino.quote: At Cape Mendocino the necessary examinations were made to select a proper site for the light-house authorized by Congress, and upon approval of the plans and estimates the work was commenced... On the 8th of September, during a fog, the steam tender Shubrick, whilst on her way from San Francisco with materials for the structure, went ashore about thirty miles below Cape Mendocino, and will probably prove a total loss.
Cape Mendocino.establishes: Construction begun in 1867 and the loss of the lighthouse tender Shubrick with Cape Mendocino materials, 8 September 1867. One man drowned landing brick. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Cape Mendocino.quote: In November everything was ready for the exhibition of the light, and after proper notice it was shown for the first time on the night of December 1, 1868, and this important and very difficult work was considered as completed.
Cape Mendocino.establishes: CAPE MENDOCINO FIRST LIGHTED: the night of 1 December 1868. The same passage records that the tower was manufactured in San Francisco, the lantern reached San Francisco February 1868, the lens was shipped 5 August 1868, and everything was landed at Eureka and hauled some forty miles to the cape. Verified against the page image (leaf n517).

Cape Mendocino.quote: 401. Cape Mendocino, sea-coast of California. — The brick dwelling-house at this station was so badly injured by an earthquake on March 2, that it was deemed necessary to pull it down, and erect in its stead a double house of wood.
Cape Mendocino.establishes: Earthquake of 2 March 1871 destroyed the Cape Mendocino keepers' dwelling. Verified against the page image (leaf n564).

Cape Mendocino.quote: 438. Cape Mendocino, sea-coast of California. — There is a settlement of the ground, caused by an earthquake, in the ravine to the north of the tower, the limits of which are well defined by a continuous crack in the earth. The south line of this crack passes through one end of the cement retaining-wall and within 15 feet of the tower... A suit, Buhne vs. Chism, to eject the light-house keepers at this station — a suit involving the title to the site — was decided on the 10th of October in favor of the United States.
Cape Mendocino.establishes: Earthquake ground failure within 15 feet of the tower, and the title suit Buhne vs. Chism decided 10 October 1872/73 for the United States. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Point Reyes.quote: A contract was entered into recently, for erecting the light-house at Punta de los Reyes; but the work was not commenced, in consequence of difficulty growing out of a claim to the land selected as the site for the light-house.
Point Reyes.establishes: The Point Reyes title obstruction begins in FY1855 — fifteen years before the light was shown. Verified against the page image (leaf n268).

Point Reyes.quote: The exorbitant price for a spot valueless for any other purpose, which has been demanded by the owners of the rancho on which the point is situated, has been for several years the sole obstacle in the way of establishing a light-house there.
Point Reyes.establishes: The Board's explanation for the delay: the rancho owners' price. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Point Reyes.quote: Inasmuch as the cost of condemnation would have been nearly if not quite as great, and the delay very considerable, the Board accepted this offer, and a deed has been made, which was approved by the Attorney General of the United States, the deed recorded, and the purchase-money paid; so that after negotiating for fifteen years the United States is in possession of the requisite site at the Point, and landing privileges in Drake's Bay, and the last obstacle to an early beginning of the work removed.
Point Reyes.establishes: Site finally purchased for $6,000 in United States gold coin after fifteen years of negotiation; $49,288.12 then available for the works, with $45,000 more asked. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Point Reyes.quote: The work was completed in November, and the Light was exhibited for the first time on the night of December 1, 1870.
Point Reyes.establishes: POINT REYES FIRST LIGHTED: the night of 1 December 1870. The same page records the iron tower was landed at Drake's Bay and hauled to the top of the bluff on 9 October 1870, then lowered down to the site; and that the steam fog-signal cistern holds 100,000 gallons fed by a 10,000 sq ft water-shed. Verified against the page image (leaf n564).

Point Reyes.quote: 414. Point Reyes, sea-coast of California. — An appropriation of $10,000 was made by Congress, approved June 10, 1872, for rebuilding and re-establishing the steam fog-signal station at this point, which was destroyed by fire April 28, 1872.
Point Reyes.establishes: Point Reyes fog-signal destroyed by fire 28 April 1872; $10,000 for rebuilding. Verified against the page image (leaf n572).

Pigeon Point.quote: two lights have been recommended by interested parties in California, one to mark the seacoast at a point about halfway between Monterey and San Francisco bays, near Anna Nuevo, or Pigeon Point, at an estimated cost of $36,311
Pigeon Point.establishes: First appearance of Pigeon Point / Año Nuevo in the Board's reports — as a recommendation from 'interested parties in California,' estimated at $36,311. Verified against the page image (leaf n233).

Pigeon Point.quote: Pigeon Point, sea-coast of California. — An appropriation of $90,000 was made March 3, 1871, for the erection of a first-class Light-house and Fog-signal at this point. The structures are to consist of a masonry tower, which is to be one hundred feet high, from base to focal plane. The elevation of the Light above mean sea-level will be one hundred and fifty-eight feet. The keeper's dwelling is to be a double two-story house, built of wood. Work on the above structures was commenced on the 9th of June.
Pigeon Point.establishes: Cost ($90,000, act of 3 March 1871), order (first-class), tower height (100 ft), focal height (158 ft), and start of work (9 June 1871). Verified against the page image (leaf n565 context; the same text appears in the OCR of p. 539).

Pigeon Point.quote: A steam fog-whistle has been erected on this point, and has been in operation since September 10, 1871.
Pigeon Point.establishes: Pigeon Point steam fog-whistle in operation from 10 September 1871 — over a year BEFORE the light. Verified against the page image (leaf n572).

Pigeon Point.quote: 429. Pigeon Point, sea-coast of California. — The work on the light-house at this station was resumed in July, 1872, and completed in October. It was illuminated for the first time on the 15th of November, 1872.
Pigeon Point.establishes: PIGEON POINT FIRST LIGHTED: 15 November 1872. Verified against the page image (leaf n710).

A\u00f1o Nuevo.quote: Point Ano Nuevo. — An appropriation has been made, also, for a first-order light at Point Ano Nuevo. The site selected is an island about a quarter of a mile distant from the main land, and has been reserved for light-house purposes by the President of the United States. Nevertheless, the owners of the rancho claim the title to the island to be vested in them.
A\u00f1o Nuevo.establishes: A first-order LIGHT was appropriated for Año Nuevo Island and a presidential reservation made, but title was contested. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

A\u00f1o Nuevo.quote: it is doubtful which of the two, the island at Point Ano Nuevo, or Pigeon Point, six miles distant, would best subserve the interests of navigation. But both points are upon the same rancho, (Punta del Año Nuevo,) and it was not possible to obtain a site at either upon such terms as the Board could agree to.
A\u00f1o Nuevo.establishes: The Board treated Año Nuevo and Pigeon Point as alternatives on the same rancho; the choice of Pigeon Point for the light, and Año Nuevo for a fog-signal only, follows from this. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

A\u00f1o Nuevo.quote: 408. Año Nuevo Island, sea-coast of California. — A steam fog-whistle and keeper's dwelling have been constructed on this island, and it has been in operation since the 29th of May of this year.
A\u00f1o Nuevo.establishes: WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BUILT at Año Nuevo in Era 1: a steam fog-whistle and keeper's dwelling, in operation from 29 May 1872. NO light. Año Nuevo appears in every later Era-1 fog-signal list and never in a first-lighting table. Verified against the page image (leaf n571).

Point Hueneme.establishes: Point Hueneme was already an authorized but unbuilt station in the 1858 Light List — sixteen years before it was lit. Verified against the page images (leaves n481, n482).

Point Hueneme.quote: Point Hueneme, sea-coast of California, east side of southern entrance to Santa Barbara Channel. — An appropriation of $10,000 is recommended for the erection of a first-class steam Fog-signal at this point, which is directly opposite Anacapa Island. With a first-order Light on the eastern end of Anacapa Island, and a steam Fog-signal on the western extremity of Point Hueneme, the southern approaches to Santa Barbara Channel will be well marked, and the navigation of the waters of that portion of California coast rendered less dangerous.
Point Hueneme.establishes: WHY: the Board's original 1871 scheme was a LIGHT on Anacapa and only a FOG-SIGNAL at Hueneme. The Anacapa light was never built; Hueneme got the light instead. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Point Hueneme.quote: Point Hueneme, Santa Barbara Channel, California. — An appropriation of $10,000, approved June 10, 1872, has been made for the establishment of a first-class fog-signal at this point.
Point Hueneme.establishes: $10,000 appropriated 10 June 1872 for a fog-signal. Verified against the page image (leaf n571).

Point Hueneme.quote: 422. Point Hueneme, entrance to the Santa Barbara Channel, California. — As in the preceding case proceedings of condemnation of the site selected and surveyed are still progressing. An appropriation, made June 10, 1872, of $22,000, is available for constructing a light-house at this locality.
Point Hueneme.establishes: By 1873 the project had become a LIGHT-HOUSE with $22,000 available (act of 10 June 1872). Verified against the page image (leaf n710).

Point Hueneme.quote: 435. Point Hueneme, sea-coast of California. — The light at this station was exhibited for the first time on the evening of December 15, 1874. Plenty of water for irrigation is had from the artesian well on the reservation. It is important that a steam fog-signal should be established here. The numerous passenger and other steamers, in going up and down the coast, pass inside Anacapa Island, and very near the coast, which here makes a considerable elbow. The land at this point is quite low, and is so for ten miles inland, so that it is difficult to see it if there is any fog.
Point Hueneme.establishes: POINT HUENEME FIRST LIGHTED: the evening of 15 December 1874 — and the Board's own statement of why the point is dangerous. Corroborated by the report's own table, p. 730: 'Point Hueneme | On the main-land, at the eastern entrance to the Santa Barbara Channel. | December 15, 1874.' Both verified against the page images (leaves n845 and n786).

Point Fermin.quote: 366 | San Pedro | On Point Fermin | ...... | Authorized.

Point Fermin.quote: Point Fermin, sea-coast of California, near entrance to San Pedro Harbor. — An appropriation of $25,000 is recommended to establish a fourth-order Light-house and a steam Fog-signal at this point to mark the approaches of San Pedro Harbor... The number of vessels navigating near the southern coast of California, between there and San Diego, and passing through the Santa Barbara Channel, has been greatly increased within the last two years. All Coast steamers stop at San Pedro, near Wilmington, the port of Los Angeles, and a Light-house and Fog-signal, as guides to the entrance of the harbor, are of great importance.
Point Fermin.establishes: WHY POINT FERMIN WAS BUILT, in the Board's own words: the growth of the San Pedro / Wilmington / Los Angeles coastal steamer trade. Order recommended: fourth. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Point Fermin.quote: 432. Point Fermin, coast of California. — An appropriation of $20,000 was made June 10, 1872, for the purpose of erecting at this station a fourth-order light house. As it was found impossible to secure the proper site from the owners (several being minor heirs) by purchase, it was found expedient to secure the same by condemnation under the laws of this State. Suit was accordingly brought for that purpose, which terminated favorably to the United States on the 4th day of November, 1873. The plans for the structure having been prepared, on the 21st of February of this year the work was commenced.
Point Fermin.establishes: Appropriation $20,000 (10 June 1872), condemnation judgment 4 November 1873, construction begun 21 February 1874. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

But Point Pinos is only a harbor Light, and the coasting steamers take their departure from Piedras Blancas, and keep so far out that Point Pinos Light is not seen, and it may be considered that there is no sea-coast Light between Point Conception and Pigeon Point, which are nearly two hundred miles distant. An appropriation of $75,000 is submitted for the erection of a first-order Light and Fog-signal at Piedras Blancas.
Piedras Blancas.establishes: WHY PIEDRAS BLANCAS WAS BUILT, in the Board's own words: a two-hundred-mile dark stretch of sea-coast. Cost sought: $75,000, first order. Piedras Blancas.quote: 438. Piedras Blancas, sea-coast of California. — The tower at this station was completed and the light put in operation on February 15th, 1875, the keepers being accommodated in the shanties built for use of the mechanics and laborers.

\u2b50 MARE ISLAND.quote: and the other on the southern end of Mare island, to aid vessels passing through the straits of Carquines and San Pablo bay, and mainly to serve as a guide to the navy yard at Benicia — estimated cost, $9,989.

\u2b50 MARE ISLAND.quote: Straits of Carquinez, California, between the Bay of San Pablo and Suisun Bay. — An appropriation was made for the erection of a light-house on Mare Island; but as that location was not suited to the wants of navigation, the money was turned into the treasury, and a re-appropriation is submitted on the estimates for this point as the proper one.

\u2b50 MARE ISLAND.quote: Mare Island, entrance to the straits of Carquines, California. — An appropriation of $10,000 is recommended for the erection of a fifth-order Light at this point, to mark the approaches to Carquines Straits. The erection of a Light-house at this point has been strongly urged for many years.
\u2b50 MARE ISLAND.establishes: ORDER OF LENS SOUGHT: fifth order. Cost sought: $10,000. And the Board's own acknowledgment that Mare Island had been 'strongly urged for many years' — consistent with its own 1857 recommendation. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

\u2b50 MARE ISLAND.quote: Entrance to the Straits of Karquines, California. — An appropriation of $20,000, approved June 10, 1872, was made for the erection of a light-house and fog-signal to mark the entrance to the Straits of Karquines. A site on the southern shore, opposite Mare Island, having been recommended by the local officers and others, surveys were made there, but none suitable was found, and the engineer of the district has been ordered to locate the light on the southern end of Mare Island.
\u2b50 MARE ISLAND.establishes: THE DECISION. Appropriation $20,000, approved 10 June 1872, for a light-house AND fog-signal. The Board first surveyed the SOUTHERN (Contra Costa) shore opposite Mare Island, found nothing suitable, and then ordered the light onto the southern end of Mare Island itself. Verified against the page image (leaf n572).

Mare Island, entrance to Straits of Karquines. — The light-house of this station was completed by the 15th of July, although it was not quite ready for lighting at that date. An attempt was made to obtain water by digging a well, but without success. The point south of the dwelling was cut down and graded, a retaining-wall, built of rock to above high-water mark, forming a plateau for fog-signal. Inclines have been constructed from this plateau and from the plane of the dwelling to the boat-landing; windlasses, provided with turn-table and car, were set up on each. The erection of the necessary building for the fog-bell, and the sinking of a well for the weight of the machinery, still remains to be done.

\u2b50 MARE ISLAND.quote: 450. Mare Island, Straits of Karquines, California. — Repairs have been made at this station, consisting of a strong stone sea-wall to protect the fog-bell tower. The foundation of this tower needs strengthening; this work will be done as soon as practicable.

East Brother.quote: 434. East Brother Island, San Pablo Bay, California, opposite Point San Pablo. — In consequence of the apparent increasing litigation to gain possession of a site on the main-land for light-house purposes, an examination was made of the East Brother Island to ascertain if it would be a suitable locality. A special report was made by the district officers in regard to its advantages, and the selection was approved by the Board. Proposals were invited for building a light-house and a fog-signal building; for making the necessary excavations, and executing the grading; also, for building a retaining-wall. The lowest bid was accepted, and the work was commenced near the end of July.
East Brother.establishes: WHY EAST BROTHER EXISTS: the Board could not get a mainland site at Point San Pablo because of litigation, so it moved the station onto the island. Work begun late July 1873. Verified against the page image (leaf n710).

East Brother.quote: 447. East Brother Island light-station, off Point San Pablo, and the straits separating San Francisco and San Pablo Bays. — An appropriation of $30,000 was made by Congress March 3, 1873, "for a light-house and steam fog-signal at Point San Pablo, California." In consequence of the litigation necessary to obtain a site on the mainland, it was determined to erect the light-house and fog-signal structures on East Brother Island, which is immediately opposite and about a quarter of a mile distant from Point San Pablo. A contract was made to blast off the top of the rock, build a sustaining-wall around the same, and erect the light-house and fog-signal. They were completed in February and the light was exhibited for the first time on the evening of 1st of March of this year. A subsequent contract was made for building the cistern, water-shed, wharf, tramway, and out-houses. This contract was completed in April and the steam fog-signal was put in operation on May 1st of this year.
East Brother.establishes: EAST BROTHER FIRST LIGHTED: the evening of 1 MARCH 1874; steam fog-signal in operation 1 MAY 1874; cost $30,000 under the act of 3 March 1873, appropriated for 'Point San Pablo' and spent on East Brother Island. Corroborated by the same report's table, p. 618: 'East Brother Island | On East Brother Island, off Point San Pablo, California | March 1, 1874.' BOTH verified against the page images (leaves n732 and n668).

East Brother.quote: 461. East Brother Island, in straits connecting San Francisco and San Pablo Bays, California. — Considerable repairs and renovations have been made to the light-house and fog-signal structures and machinery during the past year. The wharf has been strengthened by driving six piles, and thoroughly binding them together with 12-inch by 12 inch timbers, and iron straps and bolts. A truss bridge from the wharf to the bluff of the island, and a new boat-house, have also been built. The wharf is now 3 feet higher, and is so strengthened as to withstand any ordinary storm.
East Brother.establishes: Storm damage and reconstruction of the East Brother wharf and landing, 1875-76. Verified against the page image (leaf n834).

Yerba Buena Island.quote: 446. Yerba Buena, San Francisco Bay, California. — The fog-bell recently in use at Point Conception light-station, California, has been put in position here, and is operated by a Stevens clock apparatus. Congress at its last session made an appropriation of $10,000 for the establishment of a light-house and fog-signal on the southeastern extremity of this island; an examination for the purpose of selecting a proper site for the light-house has been made.
Yerba Buena Island.establishes: Yerba Buena's first aid was a fog-bell cast off from Point Conception, on Stevens clock machinery; $10,000 then appropriated for a light-house and fog-signal on the southeastern extremity. Verified against the page image (leaf n732).

Yerba Buena Island.quote: 448. Yerba Buena Island, San Francisco Harbor, California. — The keeper's dwelling and tower have been completed, excepting the putting up of the lantern and illuminating apparatus. When the apparatus is received it will be immediately put in place on the tower. The lens formerly in use at Yaquina light-station, Oregon, will be used at this station, and the light can be exhibited on or about the 15th of September. Congress, at its last session, appropriated $5,000 for establishing a steam fog-signal at this station. The work was commenced in June, and is nearly completed. The signal will be put in operation on the 1st of October.
Yerba Buena Island.establishes: ORDER/PROVENANCE OF THE LENS: the Yerba Buena light used the lens taken from the discontinued Yaquina Bay light-station, Oregon (discontinued 1 October 1874 per the 1875 report's own table, p. 730). The Board expected to light on or about 15 September 1875 — the actual date was 1 October. [OCR text; not verified against the page image.]

Yerba Buena Island.quote: Yerba Buena | On southeastern extremity of Yerba Buena Island, San Francisco Bay, California. | October 1, 1875.

Yerba Buena Island.quote: 460. Yerba Buena Island, San Francisco Bay, California. — The steam fog-signal mentioned in the last annual report as being nearly completed was put in operation October 1, 1875.

Trinidad Head.quote: Trinidad Head, sea-coast of California. — An appropriation for the erection of a Light-house at Trinidad Head was approved June 20, 1860, but nothing was done toward building the structures until February of this year. The materials were purchased and the work commenced in June, and the work is now progressing favorably. The Light will be of the fourth order, fixed, varied by red flashes, and will be shown from a low, square, brick tower.

Trinidad Head.quote: 418. Trinidad Head, sea-coast of California. — On the night of December 1, 1871, a fourth-order light of the system of Fresnel was exhibited for the first time from the tower built on the southern slope of Trinidad Head. The structures built consist of a pyramidal tower on a square base, 18 feet high from the ground-line to focal plane; a dwelling for the keeper, and a cistern.

Point Arena.quote: At Point Arena and Point Reyes examinations have been made with a view to determine the proper sites for light-houses authorized by Congress, and no time will be lost in securing the establishment of proper lights at the earliest practicable day.

On July 30, last, the workmen with all the necessary tools, together with a quantity of cement and lime, reached the Point. ... A contract has been made for furnishing five hundred thousand bricks to be made on the ground. The first kiln was burnt in the spring of this year, but upon inspection were found not to be up to the prescribed standard, and were therefore rejected.

The light was exhibited for the first time, May 1, 1870. The apparatus is of the first order, fixed in a tower 100 feet high from base, and the height of the light above the mean level of the sea 150 feet.

Point Arena.establishes: Point Arena steam fog-whistle in operation 25 November 1871. Verified against the page image (leaf n572).

Twelfth District (context for all Califo.quote: At the date of the last annual report this district comprised the entire Pacific coast of the United States, but upon the recommendation of the board, the honorable Secretary of the Treasury authorized the division of that coast into two districts, the 41st parallel of latitude being the line of separation, and which division was carried into effect on the 1st of July, 1867.

Any Era-1 'twelfth district' citation must be read against this date. Verified against the page image (leaf n302).

Pacific coast programme (context).quote: The contract made by the Treasury Department, in 1851, for building eight light-houses on the Pacific coast, has proved a fruitful source of difficulty, delay, and expense. ... after the structures had been erected according to the terms of the contract, (as certified by the officers charged with their inspection,) and the lanterns and illuminating apparatus had arrived at San Francisco, it was found that no attention had been paid to the dimensions of the towers in constructing the lanterns; and as a consequence, all of the towers except two have either been taken down and rebuilt entirely, or remodelled at a considerable expense, for the purpose of adapting them to the lanterns and apparatus.
Pacific coast programme (context).establishes: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT EXPLANATORY PASSAGE FOR THE 1853-1856 CALIFORNIA LIGHTING DATES: the eight 1851-contract towers (Alcatraz, Battery/Fort Point, Farallones, Humboldt, Point Loma, Point Pinos, Point Conception, Santa Barbara and the northern ones) were finished before lanterns that did not fit them, and all but two had to be rebuilt or remodelled. This is why 'tower completed' (1853) and 'light exhibited' (1854-1856) are years apart. Verified against the page image (leaf n268).

The tower was received at the site on July 16, and was erected during August. The lens furnished was found to be too large for the space provided for it, therefore it was necessary to procure another, which reached the station in January, 1891, and was put in place during February. On March 23, the light was exhibited for the first time. It is of the third order, flashing red and white alternately, with twenty seconds' interval between the flashes. An electrical call-bell system was put up connecting the tower with both dwellings.

Roe Island, Suisun Bay.quote: 814. Roe Island, Suisun Bay, California.—Contracts for the construction of this station were let to Mr. M. A. Graham for the ironwork, and to the California Bridge Company for the construction of the buildings and wharf. Both contractors completed their work in a satisfactory manner and within the specified time. A small building, to contain the fog-bell machinery, was built on the outer end of the wharf, and a bell was purchased and hung.
